wins: Collected comprehensive host reconnaissance and identified the primary services running on the target, yielding the full list of open ports.
Mapped the network perimeter successfully, confirming reachable entry points for further exploitation attempts.
fails: Could not gain interactive shell access despite high-reward reconnaissance, indicating a gap in exploitation technique execution.
Privilege escalation phase stalled after initial foothold attempt, preventing persistence or lateral movement.
key_outcomes.summary: Reconnaissance excelled, but exploitation and post-compromise stages remain unresolved; focus on converting high-quality intel into a stable foothold.

repeated_failure_patterns.pattern: Exploit payload delivery did not result in an interactive shell, likely due to incorrect payload handling or service protections.

skill_cards.if_condition: When port 22 is open and SSH banner detected
skill_cards.then_action: Run SSH enumeration with nmap scripts

skill_cards.if_condition: When HTTP/HTTPS service exposes login form
skill_cards.then_action: Use wfuzz for credential discovery using wordlist and response length filters

skill_cards.if_condition: When service responds to crafted payload but no shell is returned
skill_cards.then_action: Automatically capture service logs and rerun payload with netcat listener for manual review

memory_ops.reason: High success rate in reconnaissance phase

next_experiments.title: Retry SSH exploitation with manual handshake
next_experiments.description: Leverage the SSH enumeration results to craft a Metasploit module with adjusted timing and authentication options; validate access with manual reverse shell to catch service defenses.

next_experiments.title: Automate HTTP login fuzzing with session handling
next_experiments.description: Use wfuzz or burpsuite intruder with captured cookies and CSRF tokens to attempt credential discovery, ensuring rate limiting by introducing delays between requests.

next_experiments.title: Implement post-exploit persistence validation
next_experiments.description: Once a shell is acquired, test multiple persistence vectors (systemd service, cron job) to confirm the environment allows sustained access.
